Subject: Marketplace reviews: SOC 2 handling, evidence refresh cadence, and what we can share (AWS/GCP)

Hi all —

We’re getting the predictable “please provide SOC 2 + pen test + encryption/audit logging evidence” requests as part of the AWS/GCP marketplace review cycles.

Before PMM responds with any attachments / links, can we align on:
1) What we can share with AWS/GCP reviewers *without* NDA (and what’s strictly NDA only)
2) How we want to handle SOC 2 report distribution (secure link, watermarking, expiration)
3) Evidence refresh cadence + who owns the cadence going forward (SOC2, bridge letter, pen test letter, diagrams)

Soojin needs a short, accurate line for listing/FAQ: e.g., “SOC 2 Type II available under NDA upon request.”

If you can reply with guidance today, I’ll update the evidence index and send a one-pager to Partnerships/PMM.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
GRC Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace reviews: SOC 2 handling, evidence refresh cadence, and what we can share (AWS/GCP)

+1 to aligning before anything goes out.

Guidance from SecEng side:

NDA required:
- Full SOC 2 Type II report (the auditor’s report + description of system + tests of controls). Do not email as an attachment. Provide via secure link (expiring) after NDA is confirmed.
- Detailed pen test report (findings). Same as SOC2.

OK without NDA (assuming reviewed language):
- SOC 2 “attestation statement” / high-level confirmation (e.g., “SOC 2 Type II completed”) and audit period dates.
- Bridge letter (if it’s a formal auditor-issued bridge letter). This is generally safer but still should be controlled distribution.
- Architecture diagrams *that do not include sensitive internal identifiers* (account IDs, internal hostnames, etc.)
- Security overview section from the packet (encryption at rest/in transit, logging, access control) with correct caveats.

Cadence suggestions:
- SOC 2: annual (obviously)
- Bridge letter: quarterly until next SOC2 report is issued
- Pen test letter of attestation: annual (or after major scope changes)
- Diagrams / evidence index: quarterly, and also at any marketplace listing/security packet refresh

I can help sanity-check the “what we can share” table once you draft.

Marcus

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:37 AM PT
Subject: Re: Marketplace reviews: SOC 2 handling, evidence refresh cadence, and what we can share (AWS/GCP)

Agree with Marcus.

Additional constraints:
- No “SOC 2 certified” language anywhere (including listings). It’s “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA.”
- Do not state we “meet all AWS/GCP security requirements” in a blanket way. We can say we support encryption, audit logging, access controls, etc.
- Evidence should be routed through a single controlled channel (Olga/GRC) so we don’t end up with multiple versions floating around.

Operationally:
- If AWS/GCP reviewers push for the full SOC2 during review, we can comply, but only after confirming NDA coverage and using a time-bounded secure share.
- For customers/prospects: same policy.

Olga, please draft the one-pager + proposed FAQ line; I’ll sign off same-day if it’s consistent.

Aisha
